comparison: Both address resolution claims (C4, C72-C74). OpenEval finds the resolution estimates well-supported by multiple FSC criteria and validation approaches. Peer reviewers express significant concern about true resolution, stating it may be 'significantly lower than 3.9 Angstroms' and request additional validation including map/model FSC and gold-standard FSC.

Both address the spherical dodecamer architecture with Td symmetry (C6, C7, C30). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this structural determination is valid. Peer reviewers specifically acknowledge this corrects previous models for the assembly.

Both address de novo model building of FrhB (C5, C32, C52, C88-C92). OpenEval finds the model building well-supported by secondary structure predictions, glycine patterns, and Fe-S cluster density. Peer reviewers directly question validity of de novo building given resolution concerns, requesting authors 'make a strong case of why the map is still of sufficient quality to build a reliable de novo model.'

Both address model validation statistics (C116-C118). OpenEval finds Ramachandran statistics reasonable for the resolution. Peer reviewers request additional validation via map/model FSC, noting concerns about overfitting and that 'Ramachandran statistics alone are insufficient validation given concerns about resolution.'

Both address cofactor composition and arrangement with distance measurements (C31, C36, C106-C112). OpenEval finds electron density for metal clusters directly observed and distances appropriate for electron transfer. Peer reviewers express concern that resolution may be 'significantly lower than 3.9 Angstroms,' affecting confidence in precise distance measurements and cofactor positioning, particularly for the de novo built FrhB subunit.

Both address F420 binding site identification (C53-C54, C57-C60, C82-C85). OpenEval finds convergent evidence from differential density, proximity to FAD, and conservation patterns validates the assignment despite weak density. Peer reviewers do not explicitly critique this finding but their concerns about overall map quality and resolution directly impact reliability of substrate binding details, especially given the acknowledged weak density for F420.

Both address structural characterization of FrhA and FrhG through homology modeling (C37-C43). OpenEval finds homology to group 1 enzymes and ferredoxin domain assignment well-supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge these findings, noting the unique iron-sulfur flavoprotein subunit and accepting overall structural organization and homology relationships, though detailed model building of FrhB remains under scrutiny.

Both address cofactor presence and basic structural features (C3, C8). OpenEval finds electron density for metal clusters directly observed. Peer reviewers acknowledge the novel iron-sulfur flavoprotein and overall structural organization without specific critique of these basic cofactor observations.

OpenEval addresses FAD binding mode, conservation patterns, and entrance channel identification (C94-C98, C65-C67). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about FAD binding details.

OpenEval addresses model validation features including hydrophobic core/charged surface distribution, hydrophobic pockets, and buried helix in FrhB (C99-C105). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific validation features.
OpenEval addresses conservation patterns across FrhB family at cofactor binding sites (C70, C86, C98). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific conservation analyses.

OpenEval addresses properties contributing to successful structure determination including Euler angle distribution, rigidity, and tetrahedral symmetry advantages (C35, C77-C81). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these data quality properties.

OpenEval addresses experimental methods including purification, data collection parameters, and image processing (C33, C113-C114, C119-C129). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
OpenEval addresses established background knowledge and prior work contextualizing the study (C1-C2, C10-C29, C71). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
